clean_source_blocks.text: Apple spent much of its WWDC keynote highlighting fixes, performance improvements, and long-requested features before unveiling its upgraded AI-powered Siri, signaling that the company wants users to see AI as just one part of a broader effort to improve its software.

For the past two years, Apple has been racing to catch up in AI while frustrations with its core software quietly added up: a design overhaul users hated, a search function that barely worked, a file-sharing feature that routinely failed, and a Health app that ignored half its user base. Apple didn’t say any of that on Monday. But the structure of its WWDC keynote said it for them, leading with fixes before features, and framing a better Siri as one item on a long list of improvements rather than the main event. At minimum, the sequencing suggests Apple believes the foundation needs shoring up before it can credibly ask users to trust it with something as consequential as AI. ---

It's that time of year again: Apple just wrapped up its WWDC 2026 keynote, where it showed off what's coming to iOS, macOS and its other platforms over the next year. WWDC, or the Worldwide Developer's Conference is typically where we see all the updates that'll be coming to iOS, macOS, tvOS and all the other disparate Apple operating systems for the next year or so. Just like any other year, the bulk of the show was focused on iOS 27, but after the divisive changes, like Liquid Glass, that came to iOS 26 last year, the company focused on refining its operating systems. There weren't many hot new features announced, but there just didn't need to be. ---

Apple’s Worldwide Developer Conference on Monday started off with an apology of sorts. Instead of jumping right into the headline news about a revamped AI-powered Siri, Apple’s senior vice president of Software Engineering, Craig Federighi spent the first stretch of the keynote on a list of repairs.

WWDC, or the Worldwide Developer's Conference is typically where we see all the updates that'll be coming to iOS, macOS, tvOS and all the other disparate Apple operating systems for the next year or so. ---

[Lähde: The Verge]
The update-filled keynote showed an AI-upgraded Siri along with new features across Apple’s operating systems.

Apple’s keynote at this year’s Worldwide Developers Conference was a big one. After months of delays, Apple reintroduced us to its AI-upgraded Siri, which will go beyond what the existing voice assistant can do by offering more personalized help. We also got a look at many other updates coming across the operating systems powering the iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

You can catch up with all the biggest news in the roundup below.

Siri is getting a bunch of AI features powered by the latest version of Apple Intelligence, which Apple worked with Google to build. Apple is calling the upgraded voice assistant Siri AI, offering the ability to have back-and-forth conversations “with detailed and engaging answers,” Apple AI head Mike Rockwell said during the keynote.

In addition to offering image editing and writing tools, Siri AI also uses onscreen awareness to pull context from what’s on your screen to answer questions. Apple is also launching a standalone Siri AI app, where you can access your conversation history. Siri AI will roll out across Apple’s devices, including the iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple is adding the ability to access its new Siri AI by swiping down from the Dynamic Island, where its responses will also appear. iOS 27 comes with a “Siri Mode” in its Camera app, too, which can recognize objects in your viewfinder and tell you more about them.

There’s also a new opacity slider for Apple’s polarizing Liquid Glass design. Apple says iOS 27 will be supported by the iPhone 11 and up.

Apple’s bringing an AI-heavy update to macOS 27 Golden Gate, too. It’s building Siri into its Spotlight menu, allowing you to ask questions directly in the search bar and select files to ask about.

Similar to iOS 27, the latest version of macOS will allow you to adjust its Liquid Glass design with a new slider. Apple is making the window corner radius tighter in macOS 27 and is bringing back colorful sidebar icons.

During the keynote, Apple showed off a bunch of handy new features for Safari, including a new tab management feature that will use AI to organize all your open webpages by topic.

There’s a new “Notify Me” feature that will allow you to ask Safari to alert you to changes on a webpage — such as if a product you’ve been eyeing comes back in stock — and a way for Safari to automatically update your compromised passwords for you

---

It's a Wrap from WWDC 2026 that was all about Siri and Apple Intelligence coming across Apple OSes.

Thanking developers, Tim Cook says: "I truly believe the best is still ahead," Cook says in this video. He talks about how Apple's north star has always been creating products that serve people's needs. It's been an honor, he says and goes on thank thanking everyone for joining the company today at WWDC 2026.

You can then use Apple's foundational models to generate more types of images and use them as things like Message backgrounds or lock screen wallpapers. You can use the new Extend tool to add more background space or adjust the aspect ratio of a picture. To reframe a picture after taking it, this new tool called Spatial Reframing can help.

Apple Intelligence can group notifications into updating alerts for single activities. The Home app can also use footage from compatible cameras to generate descriptions. Shortcuts to go easier.

Siri AI will be available in English to start, but Apple says support for more languages coming "quickly."

payload.title: Apple painotti WWDC:ssä korjauksia ennen tekoäly-Siriä
payload.summary: Apple käytti WWDC 2026 -avauspuheenvuorossaan paljon aikaa ohjelmistojensa korjauksiin, suorituskykyyn ja pitkään odotettuihin parannuksiin ennen uudistetun tekoälyä hyödyntävän Sirin esittelyä.
payload.content:
Apple esitteli maanantaina WWDC 2026 -tapahtuman avauspuheenvuorossa tulevia ohjelmistopäivityksiään, mutta tilaisuuden painotus oli poikkeuksellisen selvä: yhtiö nosti ensin esiin korjauksia, suorituskykyparannuksia ja käyttäjien pitkään toivomia muutoksia, ja vasta sen jälkeen uudistetun tekoälyä hyödyntävän Sirin.

## Korjaukset nousivat etualalle

WWDC on Applen vuosittainen kehittäjätapahtuma, jossa yhtiö esittelee yleensä seuraavan vuoden aikana iOS:ään, macOS:ään, tvOS:ään ja muihin käyttöjärjestelmiinsä tulevia uudistuksia. Tänä vuonna huomio kohdistui erityisesti iOS 27:ään ja yhtiön käyttöjärjestelmien viimeistelyyn.

Avauspuheenvuoron alku ei rakentunut pelkästään uusien ominaisuuksien varaan. Applen ohjelmistosuunnittelusta vastaava johtaja Craig Federighi käytti ensimmäisen osan esityksestä korjausten läpikäyntiin. Tämä loi kuvan siitä, että Apple pyrkii vastaamaan käyttäjien kokemaan turhautumiseen ennen kuin se pyytää heitä luottamaan uusiin tekoälytoimintoihin.

Taustalla on ollut kritiikkiä yhtiön ohjelmistojen perustoiminnoista. Lähdeaineiston mukaan käyttäjiä ovat hiertäneet muun muassa kiistelty käyttöliittymäuudistus, heikosti toiminut haku, epäluotettavaksi koettu tiedostojen jakaminen sekä Health-sovelluksen puutteet osalle käyttäjistä. Apple ei esittänyt asiaa tällaisena ongelmalistana, mutta tapahtuman rakenne korosti käytännön parannusten merkitystä.

## Siri jäi osaksi laajempaa viestiä

Apple on viime vuosina pyrkinyt kuromaan kiinni kilpailijoitaan tekoälyssä. Siksi uudistetun, tekoälyä hyödyntävän Sirin odotettiin olevan tapahtuman selvä pääuutinen. Esityksessä se kuitenkin asemoitiin yhdeksi osaksi laajempaa ohjelmistojen parannuspakettia.

Tämä kertoo varovaisemmasta viestistä: Apple haluaa näyttää, että tekoäly ei ole irrallinen lisä, vaan sen on nojattava toimivaan ohjelmistopohjaan. Tilaisuudessa ei lähdeaineiston perusteella nähty suurta määrää näyttäviä uusia ominaisuuksia, vaan painopiste oli käyttöjärjestelmien hiomisessa iOS 26:n jakaneiden muutosten jälkeen.

Applen kannalta asetelma on merkittävä. Ennen kuin käyttäjät luottavat Sirin kaltaiseen tekoälyavustajaan arjen tehtävissä, yhtiön on vakuutettava heidät siitä, että sen perusohjelmistot toimivat luotettavasti. WWDC:n avauspuheenvuoro rakensi tätä luottamusta ensisijaisesti korjausten, ei tekoälylupausten, kautta.
summary_bullets: Apple esitteli WWDC 2026:ssa tulevia ohjelmistopäivityksiään ja painotti korjauksia sekä suorituskykyä.
Uudistettu tekoälyä hyödyntävä Siri esiteltiin vasta osana laajempaa parannusten kokonaisuutta.
Tapahtuman painotus viittasi siihen, että Apple haluaa vahvistaa ohjelmistojensa perustaa ennen suurempia tekoälylupauksia.

article.source_text:
Apple spent much of its WWDC keynote highlighting fixes, performance improvements, and long-requested features before unveiling its upgraded AI-powered Siri, signaling that the company wants users to see AI as just one part of a broader effort to improve its software.

For the past two years, Apple has been racing to catch up in AI while frustrations with its core software quietly added up: a design overhaul users hated, a search function that barely worked, a file-sharing feature that routinely failed, and a Health app that ignored half its user base. Apple didn’t say any of that on Monday. But the structure of its WWDC keynote said it for them, leading with fixes before features, and framing a better Siri as one item on a long list of improvements rather than the main event. At minimum, the sequencing suggests Apple believes the foundation needs shoring up before it can credibly ask users to trust it with something as consequential as AI. ---

It's that time of year again: Apple just wrapped up its WWDC 2026 keynote, where it showed off what's coming to iOS, macOS and its other platforms over the next year. WWDC, or the Worldwide Developer's Conference is typically where we see all the updates that'll be coming to iOS, macOS, tvOS and all the other disparate Apple operating systems for the next year or so. Just like any other year, the bulk of the show was focused on iOS 27, but after the divisive changes, like Liquid Glass, that came to iOS 26 last year, the company focused on refining its operating systems. There weren't many hot new features announced, but there just didn't need to be. ---

Apple’s Worldwide Developer Conference on Monday started off with an apology of sorts. Instead of jumping right into the headline news about a revamped AI-powered Siri, Apple’s senior vice president of Software Engineering, Craig Federighi spent the first stretch of the keynote on a list of repairs.
